name: libxmi
desc: C/C++ function library for rasterizing 2D vector graphics
why: GNU vector graphics rasterizer library with a rare pedigree, a close call that could yield pictures from code.

brief.what_it_is: GNU libxmi is a C/C++ function library that rasterizes 2-D vector graphics. Its input is 2-D graphical primitives, including wide polygonal lines, circular and elliptical arcs, and polygons to fill or texture, along with line styles such as multicolored dashing patterns. Its output is pixels drawn into a user-supplied matrix of pixels. The page calls it a drop-in rendering module for any application that needs to scan-convert 2-D vector graphics. The page does not describe a file format or a standalone program that produces images.
brief.why_it_exists: The page presents it as a rendering module split out of the GNU plotting utilities package, so other applications can reuse the scan-conversion code. The author says it was distributed separately under the name libxmi.
brief.how_it_works: The page says libxmi uses a two-stage graphics pipeline, where the second stage is pixel-merging. The default merge is the Painter's Algorithm, in which a new pixel value replaces the old one. The page says the pixel datatype and the compositing algorithm can be redefined, and that switching to alpha compositing would be trivial.
brief.install_notes: The page says it can be installed on GNU/Linux, FreeBSD, and Unix systems. It is written in ANSI C, so any system with a C compiler should be able to build it. The page does not give build steps, dependencies, or a source download URL. It links to a 'obtaining the source code' page, but the link target was not in the text I received, so I did not follow it. The brew description and the fact that no executables are listed suggest this is a library to link against, not a command-line tool.
brief.standout: The scan-conversion code descends from the X11 sample server, written in the late 1980s by people associated with the X Consortium. It keeps pixel-level compatibility with X11 drawing functions but no longer needs an X display. The pixel type and compositing rule can be changed at compile time, so it is unusually customizable for a small rasterizer.
brief.status: Quiet. The page says the current version is 1.2, released in June 2000, and it was last updated 09 Aug 2000. I did not find a repository or commit history, so I cannot confirm any activity since 2000.
brief.caveats: The page was last updated in 2000, and no release since 1.2 is mentioned. The page does not list any commands, and the brew entry has no executables and no caveats. Output is a pixel matrix you supply, so you need your own code to turn it into an image file. The page does not state the license beyond calling the package free software. The scout note's phrase 'could yield pictures from code' is my reading of the rasterization purpose, not a claim the page makes.
quotes: It can be used as a drop-in rendering module in any application that needs to scan-convert 2-D vector graphics.
By default, libxmi uses the Painter's Algorithm (a new pixel value replaces an old one).
it has been decoupled from the X Window System: it no longer requires an X display.
fetch_log: https://www.gnu.org/software/libxmi/ - fetched OK; short page with description, history, and a note on the 1.2 release from June 2000; no commands or install steps; source-code link text present but target not exposed, so not followed
